title: U.S. House · Texas's 35th District
area: A South-Central Texas district including parts of San Antonio.

context.text: Texas redrew its congressional map for the 2026 election cycle. This is an open seat with no incumbent on the general-election ballot; Rep. Greg Casar, who represented a differently drawn 35th District, is instead running for re-election in the redrawn 37th District. Johnny Garcia defeated Maureen Galindo in the Democratic primary runoff, and Carlos De La Cruz defeated John Lujan in the Republican primary runoff.

candidates.name: Johnny Garcia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff against Maureen Galindo
candidates.currentRole: Former Bexar County Sheriff's Office deputy and SWAT hostage negotiator

summary.text: Johnny Garcia is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 35th District, an open seat. He worked in construction and then spent nearly two decades at the Bexar County Sheriff's Office, including as a SWAT hostage negotiator. He won the Democratic primary runoff over Maureen Galindo and says he is running to lower costs and make health care affordable.

background.text: Born and raised in San Antonio, on the city's West Side, where his campaign website says his mother raised him in a working-class household. He graduated from Memorial High School.
Worked construction while attending St. Philip's College, according to his campaign website.

Joined the Bexar County Sheriff's Office at 21, according to his campaign website. He began in the jail, where he says he led the Inmate Worker Program, a job-training and reintegration initiative for people in custody.

Moved to patrol and, by his account, within six months was selected for the SWAT Crisis Negotiation Team as a hostage negotiator. Ballotpedia also lists him as a public information officer for the sheriff's office.
Won the Democratic nomination for the open 35th District by defeating Maureen Galindo in the May 26, 2026 primary runoff. Redistricting moved Rep. Greg Casar to run in the new 37th District.

priorities.text: Says he is fighting for lower costs, affordable health care, and economic opportunity for working families in TX-35.
priorities.quote: An old school Democrat, Johnny is fighting for the working families in TX-35 — for lower costs, affordable healthcare, and the chance to get ahead.

positions.summary: Says he would reverse Republicans' health care cuts, always fund Medicare and support expanding what Medicare covers.
positions.quote: I’ll reverse Republicans’ healthcare cuts and invest in our rural hospitals. I’ll always fund Medicare and support expanding what Medicare covers.

positions.summary: Says tariffs have driven up prices and that they should end.
positions.quote: We need to end reckless tariffs that have driven up the price of everything from coffee to tomatoes to appliances.

positions.summary: Says ICE should focus on criminals and be held to the same standard as police.
positions.quote: ICE should be focused on criminals and held to the same standard as police.

candidates.name: Carlos De La Cruz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff against John Lujan
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Air Force veteran; small business owner

summary.text: Carlos De La Cruz is the Republican nominee for Texas's 35th District, an open seat. He is a retired U.S. Air Force veteran who served 20 years and later founded a kickboxing gym in San Antonio, and the San Antonio Report describes him as a political newcomer. He won the Republican primary runoff over state Rep. John Lujan with an endorsement from President Donald Trump, and says he is running to support Trump's agenda, secure the border, and care for veterans.

background.text: Describes himself as a "proud Air Force veteran, small businessman, husband, father, and conservative Texan with deep San Antonio roots."
Served 20 years in the U.S. Air Force, deploying to Afghanistan, Iraq, and the U.S.-Mexico border.
After leaving the military, he and his wife founded a kickboxing gym in San Antonio; his wife is a VA nurse practitioner, according to his campaign website.
Is the brother of U.S. Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R), according to Ballotpedia News. The San Antonio Report describes him as a political newcomer.

Placed second in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 27.1% of the vote, behind state Rep. John Lujan, and won the May 26, 2026 runoff. President Trump endorsed him and Gov. Greg Abbott endorsed Lujan.

priorities.text: Supports continued efforts to secure the border and equip Border Patrol agents.
Supports holding the Mexican government accountable for delivering water it owes to Texas agricultural communities.
Says he will support President Trump's agenda in Congress, including on manufacturing and trade with China.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to keep biological men out of girls' sports.
positions.quote: I'll fight to keep biological men out of our daughters' sports.

positions.summary: Says he will make sure law enforcement officers have the resources they need.
positions.quote: I'll make sure our officers have the resources they need to protect our families and restore law and order.

statements.quote: We need to continue securing our border and ensure our Border Patrol agents have the tools, manpower, and support they deserve.
statements.context: On the Mission page of his campaign site

statements.quote: Texas powers America, and I will fight to unleash our state's energy potential.
statements.context: On the Mission page of his campaign site

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site (carlosforcongress.com/mission) reviewed Oct. 19, 2026; it gives short statements per topic. No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Positions on abortion, guns, health care, taxes and tariffs were not found.
